<p>Development of Two High-Energy Bus ‘Cores’
For rapid support of low-trl and Educational Payloads 
	</p>
<p>Avery Brock, EE</p>
<p>The TechEdSat NOW Team:</p>
<p>Marcus Murbach PI, Seth Schisler PM, A. Salas, S. Krzesniak, M. Mooney-Rivkin, T. Stone, , J. Alvarellos,  S. Zuniga,            K. Boateng, A. Rehman, T. Hector</p>

<p></p>
</div>
<div class="slide-content"><p>TechEdSat Stack Architecture</p>
<p>3</p>
<p>TechEdSat Stack Architecture:</p>
<p>PC/104 perimeter PCBs, non-standard interconnects </p>
<p>Discrete sub-systems stacked and wired together</p>
<p></p>
<p></p>
<div class="embedded" id="slide3_rId3"></div>
<div class="embedded" id="slide3_rId4"></div>
<p>Benefits:</p>
<p>Very open standard provides extreme payload flexibility</p>
<p>Makes design of and integration with structure easy</p>
<p>Drawbacks:</p>
<p>Hand-wiring of system is complex and time consuming</p>
<p>Difficult to debug, harnessing is sub-optimal</p>
<p></p>
<p></p>
<p></p>
<p>CubeSat Developers Workshop 2023 – NOW Bus Cores</p>
<div class="embedded" id="slide3_rId5"></div>
</div>
<div class="slide-master-content"><p></p>
<p></p>
</div>
<div class="slide-notes"><p></p>
<p>3</p>
</div>
<div class="slide-content"><p>TechEdSat Power Architecture</p>
<p>4</p>
<div class="embedded" id="slide4_rId3"></div>
<p>Inhibiting:</p>
<p>ISS PSRP-approved inhibit scheme using triple-redundant mechanical switches</p>
<p>15 to 30 minute activation delay for radios, instant-on or set delay for payloads and other systems</p>
<p>Power Management:</p>
<p>Direct connection of batteries to PDS and solar arrays (panel-based MPPT)</p>
<p>ISS-approved COTS camera batteries have built-in protections and charge limiting</p>
<p>Six-inch spacing requirement between 10Ah packs per ISS PSRP</p>
<p>Design has functioned for 20+ missions, but TES is outgrowing its power architecture</p>
<div class="embedded" id="slide4_rId4"></div>
<div class="embedded" id="slide4_rId5"></div>
<p>Mechanical Inhibits</p>
<p>Charge Port</p>
<p>Battery Pack Set A</p>
<p>Battery Pack Set B</p>
<p>CubeSat Developers Workshop 2023 – NOW Bus Cores</p>
</div>
<div class="slide-master-content"><p></p>
<p></p>
</div>
<div class="slide-notes"><p></p>
<p>4</p>
</div>
<div class="slide-content"><p>TechEdSat ‘Cores’</p>
<p>5</p>
<div class="embedded" id="slide5_rId3"></div>
<p> </p>
<div class="embedded" id="slide5_rId4"></div>
<div class="embedded" id="slide5_rId5"></div>
<div class="embedded" id="slide5_rId6"></div>
<p>‘Tardigrade’ All-In-One Solution (Second-Gen)</p>
<p>‘Powerboard’ Core C&amp;DH and Power (First-Gen)</p>
<p>Combined C&amp;DH and EPS/EPD single-board modules, i.e. Spacecraft ‘Cores’</p>
<p></p>
<p>Powerboard has been the backbone of every TES mission, with Tardigrade recently supplementing</p>
<div class="embedded" id="slide5_rId7"></div>
<p>6U TES-10</p>
<p>2U TES-7</p>
<p>CubeSat Developers Workshop 2023 – NOW Bus Cores</p>
</div>
<div class="slide-master-content"><p></p>
<p></p>
</div>
<div class="slide-notes"><p>C&amp;DH/Power</p>
<p>5</p>
</div>
<div class="slide-content"><p>TechEdSat ‘Cores’</p>
<p>6</p>
<div class="embedded" id="slide6_rId3"></div>
<p> </p>
<div class="embedded" id="slide6_rId4"></div>
<div class="embedded" id="slide6_rId5"></div>
<p>‘Tardigrade’ All-in-one Solution (Second-Gen)</p>
<p>‘Powerboard’ Core C&amp;DH and Power (First-Gen)</p>
<p>40-Watt All-In-One Board</p>
<p></p>
<p>Vorago VA10820 processor</p>
<p>128KB flash, 32KB RAM</p>
<p>50 MHz ARM Cortex-M0 32 bit</p>
<p>Rad-Hardened</p>
<p>Six 2A solar panel channels</p>
<p>Channel power monitoring</p>
<p>Single battery channel</p>
<p>Power monitoring</p>
<p></p>
<p></p>
<p></p>
<p></p>
<p></p>
<p></p>
<p></p>
<p></p>
<p>External supplies and motor drivers</p>
<p>Iridium 9603, 2.4 GHz XBee3</p>
<p>Mini GPS, Thermocouple channels,      3-axis Magnetometer</p>
<p></p>
<p>A single-board satellite design that was not pursued and fully developed</p>
<p>14-Watt Power and Communication Board</p>
<p></p>
<p>ATmega328 processor - obsolete</p>
<p>32KB flash, 2KB SRAM</p>
<p>16 MHz 8-bit processor</p>
<p></p>
<p>Half the memory of Apollo Guidance, yet running full missions with two bytes of free memory </p>
<p></p>
<p></p>
<p></p>
<p></p>
<p></p>
<p></p>
<p></p>
<p></p>
<p>Four 3A solar panel channels</p>
<p>Channel voltage monitoring</p>
<p>Single battery channel</p>
<p>Voltage, discharge current monitoring</p>
<p>Power supply outputs to subsystems, driver for Exo-brake deployment</p>
<p>Iridium 9602 modem</p>
<div class="embedded" id="slide6_rId6"></div>
<p>CubeSat Developers Workshop 2023 – NOW Bus Cores</p>
</div>
<div class="slide-master-content"><p></p>
<p></p>
</div>
<div class="slide-notes"><p>C&amp;DH/Power</p>
<p>6</p>
</div>
<div class="slide-content"><p>Design Limitations</p>
<p>7</p>
<div class="embedded" id="slide7_rId3"></div>
<p>Single low-voltage feed via mechanical inhibits inherently limits total system power due to I2R losses regardless of Core design</p>
<p>Existing hardware cannot support a 50W payload</p>
<p></p>
<div class="embedded" id="slide7_rId5"></div>
<p>CubeSat Developers Workshop 2023 – NOW Bus Cores</p>
</div>
<div class="slide-master-content"><p></p>
<p></p>
</div>
<div class="slide-notes"><p>Construction Limitations:</p>
<p>Arduino ProMini discontinued</p>
<p>Neither existing solution can support desired 50W payloads</p>
<p></p>
<p>7</p>
</div>

<div class="slide-content"><p>Bus System Flexibility</p>
<p>8</p>
<div class="embedded" id="slide8_rId3"></div>
<div class="embedded" id="slide8_rId4"></div>
<div class="embedded" id="slide8_rId5"></div>
<div class="embedded" id="slide8_rId5"></div>
<div class="embedded" id="slide8_rId6"></div>
<div class="embedded" id="slide8_rId7"></div>
<div class="embedded" id="slide8_rId8"></div>
<p>1. Support a multitude of bus sizes and power capabilities with a minimum of hardware:</p>
<p>0.5U, 1U, 3U, 6U-L, 6U-XL, &amp; 12U+ Bus Sizes</p>
<p>10, 20, 30, &amp; 40Ah+ battery pack configurations</p>
<p>Balloon, sub-orbital, orbital, ISS, and beyond LEO mission desires</p>
<p></p>
<p>2. Support ISS PSRP heritage compliance while also supporting new space launchers and high-energy systems</p>
<p></p>
<p>3. Explicitly support third-party ‘black-box’ payloads, i.e. provide clean standardized interfaces unused by core avionics</p>
<p>NOW bus sizes with expected payload volume in red</p>

<p>CoreStack Concept</p>
<p>12</p>
<div class="embedded" id="slide12_rId3"></div>

<p></p>

<div class="slide-content"><p>CoreStack</p>
<p>13</p>
<div class="embedded" id="slide13_rId2"></div>
<p>CubeSat Developers Workshop 2023 – NOW Bus Cores</p>

<div class="slide-content"><div class="embedded" id="slide14_rId3"></div>
<p>CoreStack Controller</p>
<p>14</p>
<div class="embedded" id="slide14_rId4"></div>
<p>CubeSat Developers Workshop 2023 – NOW Bus Cores</p>
<p>Core Features:</p>
<p>USB-C Single-Point EGSE</p>
<p>60W USB-C PD-Compliant Charging </p>
<p>Status LEDs and USB 2.0 Link</p>
<p>Multiple Processor Options</p>
<p>Inter-operable footprints for several microcontrollers</p>
<p>Teensy 4.0, 3.2 – TES Heritage</p>
<p>Adafruit Feather – SAMD21 ARM-M0, SAMD51 ARM-M4</p>
<p>Embedded Vorago ARM-M4 Rad-hard</p>
<p>Single-Board Blackbox</p>
<p>Total power system failure survival with sensor polling and final packets comms</p>
<p></p>
<p></p>
<p></p>
<p></p>
<p>Comms:</p>
<p>Iridium 9062 SBD: Commanding, Core Status</p>
<p>XBee3 802.15.4: Inter-Spacecraft Mesh Network</p>
<p>RS-422 Hardline: Inter-Spacecraft Network</p>
<p></p>
<p>Memory:</p>
<p>8Mb Program FRAM – Vorago MCU</p>
<p>4Mb Data/Configuration FRAM</p>
<p></p>
<p>Other:</p>
<p>Flight-Heritage RTC</p>
<p>GPS Signal Feedthrough</p>
<p>Standardized Board to Board Interface</p>
<p>Unconstrained serial interfaces, no GPIO limitations</p>
<p></p>
<p></p>
<p></p>
<p></p>
</div>
<div class="slide-master-content"><p></p>

<div class="slide-content"><p>CoreStack Development</p>
<p>15</p>
<div class="embedded" id="slide15_rId2"></div>
<p>CubeSat Developers Workshop 2023 – NOW Bus Cores</p>
<p>Mini PDS</p>
<p>Max PDS</p>
<p>Optimize</p>
<p>Controller</p>
<p></p>
<p></p>
<p></p>
<p>Controller</p>
<p>Complete the design and layout of new CoreStack controller; start software development</p>
<p></p>
<p>Mini PDS</p>
<p>Complete the design of and build the new single-board ISS-inhibit scheme 80W PDS and fly it</p>
<p></p>
<p>Max PDS</p>
<p>Develop the two-board 200W+ PDS stack and begin laboratory and environmental testing</p>
<p></p>
<p>Optimize System</p>
<p>Begin optimizing other TES systems to better mesh with the new CoreStack system to ease integration </p>
<p></p>
